title: Harden three properties the real run disproved: durability of released work, attempt-scoped labels, and a feed that replays terminal events
description:
Three root causes behind today's confusion, all found while driving a real epic
through ticfac on herdr. None is cosmetic; each is a durable property that is
not what the design says it is.

## 1. A released attempt's work is NOT durable, though settle says it is

`ticfac settle --release` tells the operator: "whatever this one committed stays
on its own write ref." That is only true if the ref reached origin. It had not.

Verified on run epic-pwp: `git ls-remote --heads origin | grep tick-nkf` returns
NOTHING. The attempt-2 branch exists only as a LOCAL branch in one worktree.
The commits — a clean ~1000-line extraction that builds — are one
`git worktree remove --force` away from gone, and the executor's own disposal
does exactly that when it tears an attempt down.

The push happens at `durableAttemptHead` during INTEGRATE, so an attempt that is
refused at collect never reaches it. That is precisely the attempt whose work is
most at risk, because nothing merged it.

Fix the promise or fix the code — but they must agree. Either make the write ref
durable before an attempt can be rejected holding work, or say plainly that a
released attempt's commits are local and name the worktree that holds them.

## 2. Every attempt of a tick shares one workspace label

`internal/exec/herdr/executor.go:320` labels the workspace `tickOf(spec)` — the
tick id alone. Attempt 2 and attempt 3 of the same tick therefore appear as two
workspaces both called "nkf", one holding stranded work and one live. Everything
else about an attempt IS attempt-scoped: the branch, the worktree path, the
state directory.

An operator reading the sidebar cannot tell which is which, and the one they
would reasonably close is the one holding the only copy of the work.

## 3. Following a run feed replays terminal events from earlier runs

The feed is append-only per RUN ID, and a resumed run appends to the same file.
A subscriber that starts following sees every historical line first — including
`run_finished` from the previous, failed run. A monitor that stops on
`run_finished` therefore stops immediately, reporting a failure that already
happened and is no longer true.

This bit twice in one session: the terminal event is the one a subscriber most
needs, and replaying it makes the feed actively misleading. `ticfac events
--follow` needs a "from now" cursor, or the terminal event needs a run-attempt
identity a subscriber can compare against.

Related and worth stating in the same tick: `run-epic` writes NOTHING to stdout
while it runs, so the log is not a monitoring signal either. The feed is the
only one, which raises the cost of these three defects.

acceptance_criteria: A rejected attempt holding commits has those commits durable before the rejection is recorded, or settle's message says plainly that they are local and names the worktree; verified by a test that rejects an attempt with work and then asserts where the commits can be found. Every herdr workspace label identifies the ATTEMPT, not just the tick, so two attempts of one tick are distinguishable in an operator's list. A subscriber to ticfac events --follow is not shown terminal events from an earlier run of the same run id, or can tell them apart; a test drives a resumed run and asserts a follower sees only the current run's terminal event.
